data.text:
Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has set up a coordination center to support foreign nationals affected by the severe flooding in Hat Yai district, Songkhla. The ministry is working with Thai agencies and several foreign governments — including Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines, China, Croatia, Hungary, Bangladesh, Bhutan, South Africa, and the United States — as well as the ASEAN Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance (AHA Centre) to deliver aid. Thailand also welcomes offers of personnel, equipment, and medical teams.

He said tourists stranded in flooded areas include about 4,000 Malaysians and 200 Singaporeans. Thai authorities have coordinated their safe evacuation, and some have already returned home.

The new coordination center, operating under the Emergency Flood Crisis Operations Centre (EFCOC), serves as a hub for information, assistance requests from foreign nationals, and the reception of international aid.

Sihasak said Thailand will consider any formal offers of international assistance for the recovery phase, though he remains confident the country still has sufficient internal capacity to manage the crisis.

Foreign nationals needing help can contact the center at 02-643-5264 or flood2025@mfa.go.th.

Thai citizens affected by flooding in neighboring countries may seek assistance from Thai embassies or consulates via the 24-hour emergency line 02-572-8442 or LINE: thaiconsular
